mission.subtitle: Why this matters
paragraphs: Advanced AI systems are being deployed faster than our understanding of how to make them safe, predictable, and accountable. This raises questions: how do we ensure an autonomous system will behave as intended? How do we prevent bad actors from using them for harm?
AI Safety & Governance is a student society at Western. We discuss the risks posed by advanced AI, and foster a community at Western capable of engaging with this problem across disciplines.

fellowship.title: Launch your AI safety career with our fellowship
fellowship.body: Our 8-week introductory fellowship leads small groups through an interdisciplinary course covering how AI works, why it misbehaves, and what can be done about it through technical research and governance.

network.title: University Group Network
network.body: AISW is a part of an informal network of student AI safety groups at universities from Harvard to Hong Kong, financially supported by Kairos through the [Pathfinder Fellowship](https://pathfinder.kairos-project.org/).

join.pageTitle: Apply to the Fall 2026 Fellowship | Western University
join.pageDescription: Applications are open for AISW’s 8-week Fall 2026 fellowship. Apply by September 30 to launch your AI safety career.
join.headline: Launch your AI safety career
paragraphs: Apply to our 8-week seminar-style fellowship (dinner included every week!) by September 30. Our fellowship helps you upskill so you're ready for the 120+ AI safety internships, grad programs, and other opportunities in this fast-growing field. The fellowship is interdisciplinary and open to undergrads, grad students, and anyone else in the Western University community from any department.

You might have heard that, recently, OpenAI’s AI agents have been escaping their containers and hacking other companies (the “Hugging Face incident”), or that LLMs can help scientists with certain aspects of designing toxins and viruses (*Nature*). With fewer than 0.6% of people in the AI field working on safety, more talent is needed to combat these risks.
Western AI Safety and Governance is a student group backed by Kairos, an AI safety non-profit.
The fellowship will tentatively run from October 5 to November 30. It will involve 1-2 hours of reading and a meeting each week.

faq.title: Do I need to know a lot about AI to apply?
faq.body: No! Diverse backgrounds are needed in AI safety.
bullets: Philosophy, social science, and political science students can help design laws and international cooperation frameworks surrounding AI development.
Business students can help fill the critical shortage of operations and entrepreneurship skills in AI safety organizations.
Math students are needed to tackle tough theoretical and empirical safety problems.
CS and engineering students can help build guardrails and train AIs to be aligned with human interests.

join.contact: Questions? Email us at [info@aisw.ca](mailto:info@aisw.ca), and check out our site at [aisw.ca](https://aisw.ca).

pillars.title: Technical
pillars.body: Understanding how modern AI systems work, where they fail, and what makes them difficult to align, interpret, and evaluate.

pillars.title: Policy & Governance
pillars.body: Examining the institutions, regulations, and international frameworks needed to manage the deployment of increasingly capable systems.

pillars.title: Philosophy & Ethics
pillars.body: Asking what 'safe' and 'aligned' actually mean: questions of value, uncertainty, and responsibility that technical work alone cannot answer.
